alwaysShown.question: dv105a_group_1_names
alwaysShown.why: DV-105(A) comes in only when DV-105 item 4a is answered No, so its first question is asked whenever the form is here. It follows item 4a only because that is the question before it.

alwaysShown.question: dv105a_group_1_home_1_lived_with
alwaysShown.why: Every row of the table asks who the children lived with, including the rows that follow the confidential-address box. That box is about the current address only.

alwaysShown.question: dv105a_group_1_home_2_asked
alwaysShown.why: Whether there is an earlier address does not depend on whether the current one is confidential. It follows that box only because the box is the last thing the first row asks.

alwaysShown.question: dv105a_group_2_home_1_lived_with
alwaysShown.why: Every row of the table asks who the children lived with, including the rows that follow the confidential-address box. That box is about the current address only.

alwaysShown.question: dv105a_group_2_home_2_asked
alwaysShown.why: Whether there is an earlier address does not depend on whether the current one is confidential. It follows that box only because the box is the last thing the first row asks.

alwaysShown.question: dv105a_group_2_names
alwaysShown.why: Item 3 lists the children who did not live with the first group. DV-105(A) is here because they did not all live together, so there is always a next group.

alwaysShown.question: dv105a_other_children_on_another_form
alwaysShown.why: The box under item 3 is asked whatever the last address was; it follows the table only because it is printed there.
